LHN pilots new eldercare offering, Jubiliv, at five senior-friendly units in Boon Lay
article:
Singapore-listed real estate management services group LHN Limited has launched Jubiliv — a new eldercare offering under its facilities management business segment.

It will take a service-led, rather than a property-led, approach to eldercare, and specialise in senior living, wellness programmes and home care services.

Jubiliv aims to provide a middle ground between institutional nursing homes and premium assisted living, through caregiver support and medication management.

Kicking things off is a pilot programme focusing on five senior-friendly units at 31 Boon Lay Drive — currently operating as Coliwoo Boon Lay, a 437-key co-living residence. Coliwoo is LHN's co-living subsidiary.

Through this pilot, Jubiliv will refine and advance its care model before it expands the business.

A standalone facility dedicated entirely to eldercare services is in the pipeline as the next phase of growth, LHN said in an Oct 21 media release.

At the Boon Lay property, Jubiliv will offer caregiver support and medication management to seniors seeking more support than independent living but without the intensity of a nursing home.

The five pilot units will come with built-in care services, shared amenities and a selection of active ageing activities.

They are also equipped with gerontechnology solutions and have features such as AI-powered fall detection and emergency call capabilities. These will allow the care associates to monitor the residents' well-being and respond in a timely manner.

Beyond Boon Lay, Jubiliv plans to grow its footprint through partnerships and property strategies, including working with hospitality operators, landlords and direct property investments.

This is so it can scale flexibly without being limited to properties developed from scratch.

All of Jubiliv’s care associates undergo caregiver and first aid training.

As a senior holistic care services provider, Jubiliv is looking to address what it calls a "widening gap" in Singapore’s eldercare landscape.

This comes as many existing eldercare options are nursing homes designed for seniors with high medical or dependency needs, alongside a small number of high-end assisted living facilities.

At the same time, a growing number of Singaporeans are considering retiring overseas, including in Malaysia , given the potentially lower cost of living.

"Too many seniors in Singapore are stuck choosing between a nursing home that feels overly clinical, an assisted living facility that is priced out of reach, or leaving Singapore altogether to afford a comfortable retirement," said Jess Lim, group managing director and executive director at LHN.

"Jubiliv exists to close that gap, offering seniors the independence and dignity they want, with the support their families need close at hand."

LHN noted that its move into eldercare builds on its facilities management capabilities that the group has spent years developing and applied across Reits, logistics facilities and residential portfolios.

The group also has an existing base of residential and commercial assets across Singapore, which can give Jubiliv a head start in identifying and adapting suitable properties for eldercare as it scales, LHN added.

"Our approach to Jubiliv is caregiving-as-a-service, in line with LHN's broader value proposition of uncovering complementary, untapped opportunities where our facilities management model can be applied in new ways," Lim said.

"The accommodation is simply the setting. What we're really building is the operational rigour behind consistent, quality caregiving," she continued.

Besides facilities management, LHN has three other main business segments: space optimisation, property development and energy.

Have First Resources’ earnings kept pace?
First Resources produces palm oil, mainly in Indonesia and refines it into higher-value products.
In the six months to 30 June 2026 (1H2026), revenue grew 44.5% year on year (YoY) to US$973.6 million.
Net profit attributable to owners rose even faster, climbing 57.4% to US$234.9 million, though biological asset valuations and foreign exchange gains helped lift that figure.
Strip out biological asset movements and underlying net profit grew 42.2% to US$216.2 million.
This isn’t a like-for-like comparison.
Last year’s first half included only two months of PT Austindo Nusantara Jaya, which the group bought in May 2025.
This year’s numbers include all six.
Higher sales volumes and better processing margins helped too.
Free cash flow came in at US$100.6 million, reversing an outflow of US$84.7 million from a year ago.
In tandem, the interim dividend was hiked by 77.8% to S$0.08 per share, up from S$0.045.
Investors may also have welcomed management’s view that uncertainty over Indonesia’s export rules has moderated.
None of this makes First Resources risk-free.
Export taxes, freight and interest costs all rose sharply.
Net gearing stood at 0.40x and US$115.4 million of the group’s US$229.2 million cash balance remained restricted as at 30 June 2026 under Indonesia’s revised export proceeds framework.
Management is also watching crude oil prices and developing El Niño conditions.
Related articles:

Why would investors pay more for Frencken when its profit fell?
Frencken builds electro-mechanical assemblies and plastic components for clients across the semiconductor, healthcare, automotive and industrial sectors.
At first glance, its 1H2026 results do not immediately look like those of an 87.8% winner.
Revenue slipped 0.8% YoY to S$427.8 million, while net profit attributable to shareholders dropped 3.4% to S$19.3 million.
A closer look at margins tells a more nuanced story.
Gross margin widened by 0.9 percentage points to 15.0% and gross profit grew 5.8% to S$64.4 million.
Here’s the thing: management expects the second-half revenue to beat both 2H2025 and 1H2026 and guides for higher full-year revenue and profit.
The group expects
semiconductor
, medical and automotive sales to grow.
In other words, investors appear to be paying mostly for results Frencken has promised rather than delivered.
Now Frencken has to deliver.
Free cash flow swung to an outflow of S$15.3 million from an inflow of S$50.6 million a year earlier, as working capital absorbed S$81.6 million into inventories and receivables.
Administrative and general expenses rose 9.9% and management expects industrial automation sales to fall.
Frencken does have breathing room, with net cash of S$68.8 million as at 30 June 2026.
As for the missing interim dividend, Frencken pays once a year with its full-year results, as it did last year.

How much of the building boom has Pan-United captured?
Pan-United is Singapore’s largest supplier of ready-mix concrete, which puts it in the path of the country’s building activity.
Construction activity picked up across Singapore, Malaysia and Vietnam in the first half.
Revenue grew 37% YoY to S$549.6 million and net profit attributable to shareholders climbed 49% to S$30.6 million.
Management pointed to operating leverage and efficiencies from its AiR Digital platform.
The interim dividend also rose 50% to S$0.015 per share from S$0.010 a year ago.
For context, the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) forecasts S$47 billion to S$53 billion of construction demand for 2026.
By June, S$31 billion had been awarded, with projects including Changi Airport Terminal 5 and MRT extensions.
That pipeline may explain some of the investor interest.
On the flip side, cash flow lags profit.
Free cash flow rose to S$7.4 million from S$1.0 million, but remains well below net profit.
Trade receivables grew by S$26 million alongside revenue.
Management has also flagged energy costs and supply-chain disruptions.
As at 30 June 2026, Pan-United held net cash of S$65.2 million, excluding S$39.5 million in lease liabilities.

Get Smart: Separate what’s delivered from what’s promised
A big share price gain tells you investors have grown more optimistic.
It doesn’t tell you why.
Try sorting the evidence for each winner into two piles.
The first holds what the company has already reported in earnings and dividends.
The second holds what management expects to deliver.
First Resources and Pan-United have filled the first pile with higher profits and bigger dividends.
Frencken’s valuation re-rating, by contrast, relies heavily on execution in the second half and beyond.
A stock that rises on promises needs the company to keep them.

title: MAS to develop IPO guides that distil key information from public offer documents
article:
The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) will support the Securities Investors Association (Singapore) or Sias develop IPO guides, says Minister for National Development Chee Hong Tat, who is also the deputy chairman at MAS. Chee made the announcement at Sias’ Investors Choice Awards on Oct 21.

The guides will distil key information from public offer documents, help investors identify key metrics and highlight matters that warrant a closer look. The guides will not recommend whether an IPO is a good or bad investment, Chee says

“The objective is to help investors ask the right questions and make more informed decisions,” he stresses.

“Investor empowerment should not end when a company lists,” he adds.

In addition, MAS is reviewing its regulations to see if there are ways to support more independent research of IPOs.

“An IPO marks the beginning of a company’s relationship with the wider investment community,” says Chee. “Investors need continued access to meaningful information and opportunities for constructive engagement with the companies they invest in.”

See also: JP Morgan Singapore & Asia Equity Income Fund surpasses $1 bil AUM in eight months

At the dinner, Chee also spotlighted the Equity Market Development Programme’s (EQDP) progress. The first two phases of the EQDP have laid a “strong foundation”, he says.

This year, the equities market saw average daily volumes (ADV) exceeding over $2 billion, 40% higher y-o-y, he notes.

See also: MAS places $1.45 bil with five asset managers; reviewing proposals for a fourth batch of asset managers

The market is also seeing broader participation beyond its largest stocks. Turnover for the Next50 constituents also increased by 93% from 2025. A growing number of small- and mid-cap stocks are also now able to absorb institutional flows. SGX also welcomed 10 new listings this year, raising $1.4 billion.

“Through the EQDP, our appointed fund managers have been crowding in more capital into Singapore equities,” he says. “What this means in practice is that for every dollar of public funds invested through EQDP, we are seeing more than a dollar of private capital come alongside it – a crowd-in ratio of more than 1:1 to date.”

On the proposal to consolidate listing review functions under SGX Regco first announced last October, Chee says MAS and the regulator will be issuing their consultation responses “soon” and are targeting to effect the change in January 2027.

title: Abbott to spin off baby formula business
article:
(Oct 21): Abbott Laboratories said it plans to spin off its nutrition unit into a separate publicly traded company after a series of missteps have weighed on the company’s broader performance.

As an independent company, the nutrition business will “be better-positioned to focus its resources more strategically,” Abbott said in a statement.

The planned separation won’t impact Abbott’s guidance for 2026 or guidance it will provide in January for 2027, the company said. Daniel Salvadori, executive vice president and group president of established pharmaceuticals and nutritional products, will become chief executive officer of the new nutrition company.

Abbott’s shares fell 4% in pre-market trading on Wednesday. They have fallen more than 18% since the start of the year through Tuesday’s close.

The move will allow the company’s healthcare-focused units in medical devices, diagnostics and established drugs to operate independently of the nutrition and infant formula operations that have had a number of issues in recent years. The challenges have included recalls that sparked a nationwide shortage in 2022.

The separation, a tax-free distribution to shareholders, is expected to be completed by the end of 2027. The company’s nutrition brands include Similac, Pedialyte and Ensure.

See also: US chip stocks post longest losing streak since 2008

The nutrition industry has proven difficult to navigate, with manufacturers grappling with costly recalls and mounting litigation. Abbott isn’t alone in rethinking its exposure: rival Reckitt Benckiser Plc also sought to shed its Mead Johnson infant-formula business to focus on more high performing areas.

Abbott lowered prices on some of its nutrition products at the end of last year to attract price-conscious consumers, after previously raising them to account for higher manufacturing costs.

The company last month agreed to pay US$385 million to settle US allegations related to poor manufacturing practices at two facilities, including one involving an investigation of a contaminated facility that made powder infant formula. It also agreed to pay US$670 million in August to settle some lawsuits alleging that it hid the risk that its infant formula for premature babies can cause a deadly bowel disease.

title: UK house prices decline for a third month, official data show
article:
(Oct 21): UK home prices extended their decline in August, according to official figures showing that surging borrowing costs are sapping demand.

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said average values dropped a seasonally adjusted 0.2%, falling for a third straight month.

House prices were just 0.9% higher than a year ago, reaching £273,000. On an annual basis, values are growing at their slowest pace since March, shortly after the Middle East conflict began.

“Cracks in the housing market became wider in August,” said Rob Wood, chief UK economist at Pantheon. “We expect house price inflation to hover around current rates for the rest of the year, averaging 1% in 4Q with risks to that call skewed to the downside.”

The housing market is under pressure from the Iran war’s economic fallout. Key mortgage rates have climbed close to 6%, and there’s little prospect of immediate relief with the Bank of England expected to start raising interest rates in November in a bid to get inflation back on track.

An earlier survey of property surveyors showed prospective buyers are also worried that Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey will raise taxes at his budget next week. Real estate agents expect prices to decline further in the near-term, with a particularly bleak outlook in London.

See also: Lane says greater global euro use may help ECB control inflation

Properties in the capital, where prices are still double the UK average at £554,000, suffered the largest annual declines out of any English region, the ONS said. London values fell 2.2% in the year to August, due to sharp declines in the price of flats.

title: Nvidia CEO Huang pitches Europe on all industries adopting AI
article:
(Oct 21): Nvidia Corp chief executive officer Jensen Huang pushed Europe to adopt artificial intelligence (AI) more quickly, striking a bullish note as some investors grow more sceptical about the sums being poured into the infrastructure underpinning the technology.

The Santa Clara, California-based company, whose chips have powered the AI boom, unveiled new data centre equipment, software, models and partnerships with leading companies on the continent at the event.

“For Europe to benefit from AI, and to have really created an AI ecosystem and AI economy, you need all the end markets, the end industries to adopt AI,” Huang said on Wednesday at his company’s GTC conference in Berlin. He pointed to the automotive sector, financial services and health care. “All of these different industries have to become AI companies.”

The event is part of a tour through Europe by Huang, who has been signing deals with local companies and trying to persuade the continent’s political and business leaders that AI is safe. His trip comes at a delicate moment for the industry. AI stocks have been battered during the past two weeks, and the closely watched Philadelphia Stock Exchange Semiconductor Index suffered its longest losing streak since 2008.

Jensen Huang showing the Isaac AI robot platform during his keynote address at the Nvidia GTC in Berlin on Wednesday.

See also: Getty files for bankruptcy in process that will take it private

Huang and his executive team hold GTC conferences around the globe, explaining the latest AI developments while aiming to drum up business for the company’s ever-expanding product lineup.

The new equipment includes the DSX Pod, a product that acts as a mini data centre and can be used by companies trying to get hardware up and running more quickly. With one container, customers get the server hardware, cabling and plumbing they need — already installed and tested. It only needs to be plugged in and linked to other similar units, Nvidia said.

The new design, put together by Nvidia partners such as Dell Technologies Inc, will bring down the time required to install such hardware to 14 days from the current six months, Nvidia said.

See also: SoftBank credit risk hits four-year high on AI funding strain

The container is best suited to smaller-scale deployments of less than a gigawatt. Data center projects are typically measured by the amount of energy they consume since that’s a critical input.

The chipmaker said customers across Europe are adopting its DSX AI data centre blueprint and newest processor design, Vera Rubin. Nscale Ltd, an Nvidia-backed data centre developer, is among those companies.

Nvidia, the world’s most valuable publicly traded company, has frequently cited supply chain constraints as an impediment to its growth. To combat that, Ibiden Co, Samsung Electro-Mechanics Co and Unimicron Technology Corp will help it get more substrates — the materials used to house other components.

Amkor Technology Inc will help increase the amount of chip packaging available by fourfold by the end of 2028. That material is used to encase semiconductors and connect them with other components. And KYEC Microelectronics Co will increase testing capacity. Nvidia is also helping to boost the availability of on-package optical connections, which will speed up communication between components.

With concerns growing that AI will become too difficult for humans to control, Nvidia is developing software to ensure that so-called agents — programmes that orchestrate the use of multiple models and programmes — stay within prescribed limits. Nvidia is offering up a reference design combination of hardware and software that stops agents from accessing data they shouldn’t and prevents them from giving themselves permission to do things not explicitly allowed by their designers.

In so-called physical AI — a field that includes robots — Nvidia said it’s making rapid progress. Revenue from that market rose as much as 30% to about US$11 billion in the first half of the year, the company said.

Nvidia announced a tie-up with a Siemens AG division for the deployment of AI-based advanced radiation therapy machinery. Such machines will monitor patient breathing and movements and adjust dosage dynamically.

The difficulty of deploying humanoid robots — one of the key mechanisms by which AI will become pervasive in the real world — remains a problem that many companies are working on using Nvidia’s chips and software.

The problems are so complex and expensive that the field is now only served by well-funded companies, Nvidia said.

To help open up the work to as many as possible, Nvidia is working with Agile Robots SE to create an open robotics platform that researchers can use to do development work. It’ll come with Nvidia’s Jetson Thor computer hardware inside of an Agile One SN humanoid.

In the automotive field, Nvidia said Volvo AB is making self-driving cars that use its chips. Volkswagen AG is using Nvidia products for commercial vehicles, and Bolt Technology OU is using the tech company’s software and gear for robotaxis.

title: Taiwan rejects Grab’s US$600 mil takeover of Foodpanda unit
article:
(Oct 21): Taiwanese authorities blocked Grab Holdings Ltd’s US$600 million ($767 million) takeover of Foodpanda’s local unit, a setback for the ride and food-delivery firm’s expansion plans.

Taiwan’s Fair Trade Commission rejected the deal following an antitrust review, according to a statement Wednesday. The commission said it held talks with the parties on potential merger remedies, but the proposed commitments were insufficient to address competition concerns.

Southeast Asian ride-hailing and delivery leader Grab sought to expand on the island of about 23 million people to find growth beyond its intensely competitive home market. Grab has seen sales slow dramatically as it takes steps to focus on profitability.

Foodpanda’s owner, Delivery Hero SE of Germany, has faced investor pressure for a sale or divestments to streamline the business.

Shares of Delivery Hero fell 0.8% in early Frankfurt trading. Grab advanced about 0.7% in trading before markets opened in New York.

Singapore-based Grab has struck deals to spur revenue growth beyond its core ride-hailing business, which faces intense competition from rivals such as Indonesia’s GoTo Group. It agreed to acquire a majority stake in buy-now-pay-later platform Atome Financial for US$1.49 billion last month, and earlier in the year purchased Stash Financial for an enterprise value of US$425 million.

See also: SpaceX, Tesla boards to study potential US$3.5 tril merger

“We are disappointed by this outcome,” Grab said in a statement. “Grab’s core business across Southeast Asia remains robust. We will continue to focus our capital and resources on executing our growth roadmap and empowering communities across our regional footprint.”

Foodpanda’s Taiwan operations would have added about 13% to Grab’s delivery gross merchandise value and US$60 million to its 2028 adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, said Kai Wang, an analyst at Morningstar. Grab has a target of adjusted Ebitda of US$1.7 billion for that year.

“This will only make a minor dent to Grab’s overall operations,” Wang said.

title: Finance leaders spar over AI bubble after warning by Griffin
article:
(Oct 21): Top finance and investing executives pushed back against suggestions of a bubble in artificial intelligence (AI), after billionaire Ken Griffin warned that investors in the industry should be prepared for setbacks.

Deutsche Bank AG chief executive officer Christian Sewing, speaking in an interview at the Berlin Global Dialogue, said he sees no reason to worry about a sharp reversal in asset prices any time soon. BlackRock Inc CEO Larry Fink argued in favour of pushing ahead with the rapid build-out of AI data centres, saying any delays could threaten economic growth and stoke inflation by driving up computing costs.

“Overall, I don’t think that we are living in a bubble which is bursting,” Sewing said on Bloomberg Television on Wednesday. “Do we see the one or the other setback, also with individual companies? That can happen.”

Investor anxiety over the durability of the AI boom surged in recent weeks amid fears that the substantial upfront capital spending the technology needs will take longer than expected to translate into profits and productivity gains. Anthropic PBC, one of the leading AI developers, could spend US$750 billion (RM3.06 trillion) on additional computing power in the coming years, according to a Wall Street Journal report.

Griffin, whose empire includes hedge fund Citadel and market-maker Citadel Securities, warned on Tuesday that investors are “almost certainly” in a bubble as corporations are grappling with how much they want to spend on the technology.

Fink has previously waved off concerns about an AI bubble, pointing instead to supply shortages and saying demand growth has exceeded expectations. He has also warned delays in the technology’s build-out could ultimately limit access.

See also: Lenovo seeking US$2 bil loan to refinance debt at lower cost — Bloomberg

“If we don’t build out these data centres, it is actually more inflationary because the cost of compute is so high right now,” he said on Wednesday. “And the faster we can build out more data centres, the more compute we have, the faster we can bring down the cost.”

Sewing, who has emerged as one of the most influential business leaders in Germany, said the industrial application of AI is “the chance of the century” for his home country, if it gets the regulatory framework right. Deutsche Bank itself uses the technology to increase efficiency but also to improve controls, he said.

“The fear that we are in front of a bubble is not a justified one,” Sewing said. “But what is different from a bubble is ongoing volatility,” he said, pointing to continued geopolitical tensions.

See also: Citigroup fixed-income traders post higher revenue in 3Q as rivals miss

The CEO, who has turned around Germany’s largest lender since taking over eight years ago, is one of a handful of top executives who regularly speak with Chancellor Friedrich Merz, people familiar with the matter have said. Merz hosted the German government’s first investor conference in Berlin this week, a fresh push by the embattled chancellor to revive growth in Europe’s biggest economy.

Rather than AI, Fink and Sewing both pointed to fiscal deficits as a more immediate area of concern, particularly as the AI industry competes with governments for investor money. US Treasury yields have hit multi-decade highs as markets grapple with a nearly US$2 trillion US fiscal deficit.

“We’re at a time now where we’re finally unlocking private capital, and so the competition for capital is as large as I’ve ever seen in my professional career,” Fink said.

In France, months of debate over the budget have pushed the extra yield investors demand to hold French government debt over German bonds into territory associated with the euro-area debt crisis.

“I wouldn’t call it a debt crisis at this point in time, but I think it’s a wake up call in particular for all public financing that budget disciplinary is key,” Sewing said.

title: Carrefour cuts profit forecast after riots, looting in France
article:
(Oct 21): Carrefour SA warned that the social unrest roiling France will drag on its earnings this year, the first sign of the economic impact from riots in Paris and other cities last weekend.

The grocer cut its profit outlook and other annual financial targets, sending its shares plunging by as much as 15% in Paris trading on Wednesday, the biggest intraday decline since 2017.

“There is a high degree of uncertainty regarding consumer spending trends and the conditions under which our stores will be able to open,” Chief executive officer Alexandre Bompard said late on Tuesday, describing the situation in France as unprecedented.

More evidence of the effect on businesses may emerge when retailer Fnac Darty and luxury groups Hermes International SCA and Kering SA publish sales figures this week.

Cost-of-living protests that drew more than half a million people across France turned violent over the weekend as fast-moving groups targeted hundreds of shops, smashing windows and looting merchandise.

See also: VW’s Scania hastens China e-truck push as drivers abandon diesel

While the turmoil has abated after curfews were imposed, protesters have called for another day of unrest on Saturday.

Carrefour is the first retailer to disclose the financial impact of the riots, and likely one of the most affected because of its city-centre and suburban shops in Paris and other towns.

“Weaker sales from an extended period of reduced store hours would push the profit shortfall into high single digits,” wrote Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Charles Allen.

See also: EU officials propose guardrails for insurance risk transfer boom

About 50 Carrefour stores were hit on the first day of rioting, with many looted and badly damaged, Bompard told analysts. That’s leading to lower footfall, reduced opening hours and increased costs for security and logistics, he said. Carrefour sees a maximum possible impact on profitability of around €200 million.

The ultimate hit to French growth will depend on how long disruption lasts, Charlotte de Montpellier, senior economist for France and Switzerland at ING, said in a note. “If unrest remains brief and concentrated, the macroeconomic impact could be relatively limited, but repeated protests, closures and transport disruption would make lost activity harder to recover.”

Roving bands broke into and looted businesses ranging from high-end boutiques to sporting goods stores and supermarkets.

“As we enter the critical end-of-year period for the retail sector, this situation is having a significant impact on consumer spending — which is already under pressure from rising energy costs,” Bompard said.

title: Lenovo seeking US$2 bil loan to refinance debt at lower cost — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 21): Lenovo Group Ltd is seeking a US$2 billion loan priced more cheaply than an earlier facility that it plans to refinance, according to people familiar with the matter, as banks in Asia remain eager to lend to major Chinese firms amid a dearth of deals.

 

The five-year facility, which it has launched into syndication, is priced at 75 basis points (bps) over the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR), said the people, who asked not to be identified discussing private matter.

The pricing is considerably tighter than the 110bps plus a credit adjustment spread over SOFR that Lenovo got for an equal-sized loan in 2022. The adjustment was related to the shift to SOFR from the London Interbank Offered Rate, the people added.

Lenovo is marketing the new loan as its artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure business continues to grow. The company’s revenue jumped 43% in the quarter ended June and it has boosted its fiscal year outlook. It also comes in the midst of a deal drought in the broader Asia loan market, especially from Chinese borrowers who are able to tap cheaper funding onshore.

There have been only 54 offshore Chinese loan deals completed so far this year, a 17-year low, down from a peak of 135 borrowings in the same period in 2019, according to Bloomberg-compiled data. The value of deals, however, has jumped to about US$56.1 billion from US$38.4 billion a year ago, due mainly to TikTok developer ByteDance’s US$29.6 billion loan last month, Bloomberg-compiled data showed.

ByteDance’s three-year loan, which is one of the largest dollar-denominated borrowings in Asia this year, had an opening margin of 68bps over SOFR, compared with a previous offshore facility it secured with an 85 basis point margin. Smartphone maker Oppo, meanwhile, is raising a US$1.2 billion-equivalent three-year loan offering a margin of only 50bps over SOFR.

BNP Paribas, Citigroup Inc, DBS Bank Ltd, HSBC Holdings plc and JPMorgan Chase Bank, NA Hong Kong are the coordinators of the Lenovo loan.

See also: Citigroup fixed-income traders post higher revenue in 3Q as rivals miss

Lenovo’s shares have slumped about 25% this month as concerns rise over the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure projects, but they are still up around 125% over the past year, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

Lenovo separately raised US$2 billion from a seven-year convertible bonds sale in June and plans to use the proceeds to refinance existing debt and fund share buybacks.

title: HDFC Bank probe finds that senior executives leaked secrets — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 21): An internal probe by HDFC Bank Ltd — India’s largest by market value — found evidence that two senior executives disclosed confidential business strategies and possible market-sensitive information to outsiders, according to people familiar with the matter.

The executives oversee certain key businesses and functions at the bank, according to the people, who asked not to be named discussing confidential matters.

HDFC identified the executives during an internal investigation that began after some leaders grew concerned about the possibility of information being leaked, the people said. The probe is still underway as the bank continues to examine whether the information was misused, the people said.

An HDFC Bank spokesperson acknowledged an internal review, but didn’t comment on its findings or the executives involved. “In line with our policies, an internal review into this matter is currently underway to gather and evaluate all relevant facts,” the spokesperson said by email. “Appropriate action will be taken based on the findings, once the review is complete.”

The bank said it was committed to upholding the highest standards of ethics and governance and takes reports of potential violations seriously.

The review comes at a sensitive moment for HDFC Bank, which has a market value of about US$115 billion ($147 billion) and has spent three decades cultivating a reputation for conservative management, strong internal controls and consistent profitability. The lender is preparing for its first outsider chief executive following boardroom disputes and management departures. Its share price has declined about 28% this year.

See also: BHP cuts 300 workers at Australian iron ore mines as costs rise

The probe and its findings were reported to senior management, including some members of the board, earlier this year, the people said. Both executives have since been formally informed of the findings, and it wasn’t immediately clear what disciplinary action will be taken, the people said.

The findings add to the challenges confronting Anup Bagchi, a veteran of rival ICICI Group, who is set to become HDFC Bank’s chief executive on Oct 27.

In recent months, internal divisions in HDFC have played out publicly. In March, then-chairman Atanu Chakraborty resigned abruptly, citing differences between his personal values and certain practices at the bank. An independent legal review commissioned by the lender subsequently said his concerns were not substantiated.

See also: HSBC moves to Wall Street bonus model as it cuts fixed-pay deals

Bagchi’s appointment follows the surprise decision of Sashidhar Jagdishan, the incumbent chief executive, not to seek another term. Jagdishan is stepping down after six years at the helm.

Kaizad Bharucha, deputy managing director and one of the bank’s longest-serving executives, has also asked to leave at the end of December.

Founded in 1994, as the country opened its financial sector to private competition, HDFC Bank grew into a preferred investment for international fund managers seeking exposure to India’s rising incomes and expanding consumer credit.
